payload.feature:
Fix the two platform defects decision 0046 slice (i) introduced. They are on branch fire/0046-boundary, whose head is a merge of main; the slice itself is commits 78e33d9 and 0f0c462, and CI is green on Linux and red on macOS and Windows.

Read `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i/` (the proposal, design, tasks and completion note), `docs/decisions/0046-the-boundary-is-named.md` with its addendum and erratum, and the proposed `docs/decisions/0048-the-script-directory-is-the-spawn-pin.md`, which is the ruling both defects sit under. Neither defect is a reason to weaken 0048: the pinned script's identity must stay the exact bytes of its filename components.

**1. macOS — a test that cannot run there.**
`crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/model_policy_tests.rs:3449`, in `a_filename_that_json_cannot_represent_is_refused_without_lossy_aliasing`, creates a file whose name is not valid UTF-8 to prove the pin refuses it rather than aliasing it lossily. On Linux a filename is bytes and this works. macOS refuses the create with `Os { code: 92, kind: Uncategorized, message: "Illegal byte sequence" }` — APFS and HFS+ require valid UTF-8 in filenames — and the `unwrap()` panics. The property is real and worth keeping; the test is Linux-only by nature. Guard it so it runs where a filename can be arbitrary bytes and is skipped elsewhere, with a comment saying which filesystems refuse the name and why the property still holds there by construction. Do not delete the test and do not weaken the refusal it proves.

**2. Windows — the engine overflows its stack.**
`crates/brokkr-cli/tests/agent_fallback.rs:194` asserts on a run id from the spawned `brokkr` binary's stderr; on Windows the child dies with `thread 'main' has overflowed its stack` and the assertion reports an empty run id. 145 test cases fail on Windows in this shape across several suites, all of them spawning the binary; the same suites pass on Linux and macOS. Main was green on Windows before this slice, so the slice introduced it.

The prime suspect is this slice's own script-directory revalidation and the file-map walk it added — the compiled leaf and ancestor maps, and the exact-filename-component keying — recursing without a bound on Windows path semantics, where a component may repeat in a way the Unix walk never produces. Diagnose it properly rather than guessing: reproduce it, find the recursion or the unbounded loop, and fix the cause. A depth cap that hides an infinite walk is not a fix; if a cap belongs there, it belongs there for a stated reason with the real termination condition beside it.

Every path comparison and every component split this slice added must be canonical-safe and platform-neutral: a backslash is a separator on Windows and a legal filename byte on Unix, and 0048 turns on exactly that distinction, so read its text before you touch the walk.

Add a regression test for the Windows cause that fails on Linux today if the bug were reintroduced — a pure unit test over the walk with the offending shape, not an end-to-end spawn — so the next Linux-only seat cannot miss it.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`; the four contracts this slice added are already in the tree and their bytes stay. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves from the tests' own left/right pairs. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. You cannot run macOS or Windows here; say plainly in your notes what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on instead.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: Committed 1f3546a. Made the arbitrary-byte filename test Linux-only with the APFS/HFS+ explanation; exact filename identity remains intact. Diagnosed the Windows overflow in Clap command construction before any file walk, split argument builders, and added a pure command-tree regression that overflows on Linux before the fix and passes on a 512 KiB stack afterward. All required fmt, clippy, workspace test, self/verify compile and exact-coverage gates pass (21228/21228 lines, 3300/3300 branches, 2015/2015 functions). Frozen files and digest pins unchanged; no push. macOS and Windows execution could not be verified here: evidence is the existing CI failures, Linux GDB reproduction, and Windows cross-compiled assembly, documented in proposed decision 0048.

cargo test --workspace: 61 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed the entire delivery, 6753dd7..1f3546a, against the commission, archived slice framing and decisions 0046/0048. No correctness, simplicity or security findings. Independently reproduced the saved pre-run binary overflowing on --help with a 512 KiB stack; the repaired binary and pure command-tree regression pass. The failure precedes every bundle walk, so the command-tree regression targets the demonstrated cause. All 26 extracted argument structs preserve their fields/attributes/comments; dispatch logic is token-identical after reversing tuple wrappers. All 48 help pages and sampled required/exclusive argument refusals match. The Linux invalid-filename, literal-backslash and directory-drift regressions pass; exact filename refusal and spawn-pin enforcement remain unchanged. Formatting and both self/verify bundle compiles pass. Inspected retained clippy, workspace-test and exact-coverage evidence: 61 successful suite summaries, 1266 passing tests, and 21228/21228 lines, 3300/3300 branches, 2015/2015 functions. Frozen files and witness/compose pins are unchanged. Native macOS and Windows execution could not be verified here; relied on the retained platform CI failures, Linux reproduction/GDB trace and Windows assembly frame reductions (925160 to 210064 bytes; update builder 1058088 to 218608), not a claim of native success. No repository edits, commits or task changes; only this required result file was written.
